task_instance: Diagnose and fix a Hibernate ORM / Jakarta Persistence N+1 query problem in plain Java: build a minimal JPA model (Order with a lazy @OneToMany collection of OrderLine), reproduce the 1+N statement pattern when the lazy collection is touched, apply the skill's JOIN FETCH fix, and verify the before/after SQL statement counts in an integration test against a real SQL engine.
evidence: Built a Maven project (JDK 21, Maven 3.9.11) under the work dir with Hibernate ORM 6.6.4.Final + H2 2.3.232 + JUnit Jupiter, repo installed work-locally via -Dmaven.repo.local=./.m2. Entities follow the skill's rules: OrderLine.@ManyToOne declared fetch=LAZY (overriding the EAGER default, rule 1), Order.@OneToMany kept LAZY, SEQUENCE ids with allocationSize=50 (rule 5), deliberate id-based equals and class-constant hashCode (rule 6). persistence.xml enables hibernate.generate_statistics. Test NPlusOneTest seeds 5 orders x 3 lines, then compares SessionFactory Statistics.getPrepareStatementCount() across two code paths exactly as tooling-and-versions.md prescribes. Command run: 'mvn -B -Dmaven.repo.local=$(pwd)/.m2 test'. Output: 'ANTI-PATTERN prepared statements = 6' (1 query for orders + 1 lazy init per order = 1+N) and 'JOIN FETCH prepared statements = 1' (select o from Order o left join fetch o.lines collapses to a single statement; Hibernate 6 auto de-duplicates roots). Final build: 'Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0' and 'BUILD SUCCESS'. Files produced: pom.xml, src/main/java/com/acme/Order.java, src/main/java/com/acme/OrderLine.java, src/main/resources/META-INF/persistence.xml, src/test/java/com/acme/NPlusOneTest.java, plus compiled classes under target/. Note on fidelity: the skill prefers Testcontainers against the production DB engine over H2; Docker/Testcontainers were not used (would require container runtime and network), so verification ran against the H2 in-memory SQL engine, which still exercises the real JDBC statement path and proves the diagnose+fix+statement-count deliverable. Skill reference files (fetching-and-n-plus-one.md, tooling-and-versions.md) were all present next to SKILL.md.
